    Author: PostskjermPostskjerm 44544 silver badges1616 bronze badges
    SUMMARY: The sequence \(\{1, 1, -1, -1, 1, 1, -1, -1, \dots\}\) can be mathematically expressed in several ways. Here are some effective formulas that capture its alternating pattern of two 1s followed by two -1s:

1. \( a_n = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2} \)
2. \( a_n = (-1)^{\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor} \)
3. \( a_n = \cos(n \pi/2) + \sin(n \pi/2) \)
4. \( a_n = \sqrt{2} \cdot \sin\left((2n+1)\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \)

These expressions utilize properties of powers and periodic functions to generate the desired sequence. The first two formulas leverage the even and odd nature of integers to alternate between 1 and -1 effectively. The last two formulas use trigonometric functions to achieve the same result. For a more detailed exploration of these expressions, you can refer to the original discussion [here](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1696201/what-is-a-mathematical-expression-for-the-sequence-1-1-1-1-1-1-1-1-dots).

$$\\begin{align}
a\_n&=(-1)^{n(n-1)/2}\\\
a\_n&=(-1)^{\\left\\lfloor\\frac{n}{2}\\right\\rfloor}\\\
a\_n&=\\cos(n\\pi/2)+\\sin(n\\pi/2)\\\
a\_n&=\\sqrt{2}\\cdot\\sin\\big((2n+1)\\tfrac{\\pi}4\\big)
\\end{align}$$
      - The sequence $a\_0=1$, $a\_1=1$, $a\_2=-1$, $a\_3=-1$, $a\_4=1$ and so on satisfies the recursion
$$
a\_0=1,\\quad a\_1=1,\\qquad a\_{n+2}=-a\_n
$$
so its characteristic equation is $t^2+1=0$. Thus the general solution is of the form
$$
xi^n+y(-i)^n
$$
The initial conditions tell that $x+y=1$ and $xi-yi=1$, thus
$$
\\begin{cases}
x+y=1\\\\[4px\]
x-y=-i
\\end{cases}
$$
that gives
$$
x=\\frac{1-i}{2},\\quad y=\\frac{1+i}{2}
$$
